features.title: Engine records the grant request's sequence number
features.spec:
CONTEXT. Kranz parks at most one capability-grant request per mission in `MissionState.pending_grant_request: Option<PendingGrantRequest>` (crates/engine/src/types.rs ~924; struct ~1037-1053, fields milestone_id, kind: GrantKind, command; serde camelCase). It is set by the reducer when folding `EventKind::GrantRequested` (crates/engine/src/reducer.rs ~170-186). The request's only unique identity is the event envelope's `Event.seq: u64`, which `apply(state, event)` has in hand. CONFIRMED DEFECT: decisions match by target text only, so a decision for one request can land on a later request with the same text. This feature only RECORDS the sequence number; later features check it.

DO:
1. crates/engine/src/types.rs is ADDITIVE ONLY (operator rule, gated by a contract check `git diff --numstat $KRANZ_BASE_SHA HEAD -- crates/engine/src/{events,types,backend,error}.rs` must show 0 deletions). Do not modify or remove ANY existing line, including doc comments, derives, attributes and trailing commas: only insert new lines. In `PendingGrantRequest`, insert after the `command` field: a doc comment saying it is the seq of the grant.requested event that parked this request (None for snapshots folded before this field existed), then `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` and `pub request_seq: Option<u64>,`. Wire name is requestSeq via the struct's camelCase.
2. crates/engine/src/reducer.rs ~181: in the `PendingGrantRequest { .. }` literal, set `request_seq: Some(event.seq)`. Check how the event variable is named in that match arm's scope. This is the only struct-literal site in the workspace (grep `PendingGrantRequest {` to confirm).
3. Do not change ControlCommand, orchestrator.rs, server, Slack or dashboard code in this feature.
4. TESTS in crates/engine/tests/reducer_test.rs (follow its existing grant tests). The new test name must contain `superseded_grant` (the contract filter; no existing test contains it): fold a log with plan approval then grant.requested and assert `pending_grant_request.request_seq == Some(<that event's seq>)`; then a second grant.requested after a grant.denied records the newer seq. Also assert a serialized state with request_seq None has no requestSeq key and a JSON PendingGrantRequest without requestSeq deserializes to None.
5. Add one line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md.

GATES before reporting, run bare with no pipes: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and `git diff --numstat $KRANZ_BASE_SHA HEAD -- crates/engine/src/events.rs crates/engine/src/types.rs crates/engine/src/backend.rs crates/engine/src/error.rs` must show 0 in every deletions column. Name any new Rust binding `authority`, never `token` (the secret scan refuses `let token = ...`). Commit your own work on the mission branch before reporting.
validationCriteria: PendingGrantRequest gains request_seq: Option<u64> (wire requestSeq) inserted as new lines only; types.rs shows zero deleted lines against the base
Folding grant.requested sets request_seq to that event's seq, and a later re-request records the newer seq (reducer test whose name contains superseded_grant)
request_seq None is omitted from serialized JSON and a legacy JSON request without requestSeq deserializes to None (test whose name contains superseded_grant)

features.title: Engine refuses grant decisions for a superseded request or a different kind
features.spec:
CONTEXT. A previous feature added `PendingGrantRequest.request_seq: Option<u64>` (crates/engine/src/types.rs ~1044), set by the reducer to the seq of the grant.requested event. Operators decide through `ControlCommand::ApproveGrant { command }` and `ControlCommand::DenyGrant { command, reason }` (types.rs ~1944-1954). The orchestrator drain loop (crates/engine/src/orchestrator.rs ~3129-3146) calls `approve_pending_grant(&command)` (~1955) and `deny_pending_grant(&command, &reason)` (~2019); both compare the target text only and copy `pending.kind` into the emitted event. CONFIRMED DEFECT: a stale decision naming text X lands on a later request for X (re-park, another milestone, or another kind).

DO:
1. types.rs is ADDITIVE ONLY (contract-gated: zero deleted or modified lines in events.rs/types.rs/backend.rs/error.rs). Insert, in BOTH ApproveGrant and DenyGrant, new lines only: `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] grant_kind: Option<GrantKind>,` and `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] request_seq: Option<u64>,` each with a short doc comment. Do NOT name a field `kind`: ControlCommand is `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "kebab-case")]` and a `kind` field collides with the tag. skip_serializing_if keeps legacy control files byte-identical (crates/engine/src/control.rs signs the serialized command).
2. orchestrator.rs: give approve_pending_grant and deny_pending_grant extra params `grant_kind: Option<GrantKind>, request_seq: Option<u64>`. If either is Some and differs from the pending request's kind / request_seq, return `Err(EngineError::InvalidState(..))` whose message contains 'superseded' and names the pending seq and kind, leaving the pending request untouched (the drain loop's existing 'ignored' OrchestratorDecision records it). Both None keeps today's text-only match (the CLI stays command-only). Update the drain loop arms.
3. Make the WHOLE workspace compile; struct-variant construction needs every field. Sites (grep `ApproveGrant`/`DenyGrant` across crates to confirm): crates/engine/src/control.rs tests (~594-930); crates/engine/src/orchestrator/live_permissions.rs (~883-889); crates/engine/tests/mission_test.rs (~5115-6175, 10 sites); crates/server/src/rest.rs (~1207, ~1223: pass None for now); crates/server/tests/host_test.rs (~1296, ~1315: add `..` to patterns); crates/cli/src/commands.rs (~1606, ~1622: None); crates/slack/src/dispatch.rs (~931, ~951: None for now); crates/slack/src/bridge.rs (~2445-2446: add `..`). Change no behaviour at those consumer sites.
4. TESTS; every new test name must contain `superseded_grant`. (a) End-to-end in mission_test.rs reusing `wait_for_pending_grant` and the fixtures of `unanswered_grant_request_times_out_to_denied` / `grant_request_cap_blocks_instead_of_looping`: two successive grant requests with the SAME target text; an ApproveGrant carrying the first request's request_seq while the second is pending is refused (pending unchanged, no grant.approved emitted, command_grants not widened); then an approve with the second request's seq and matching grant_kind succeeds. (b) Approve and deny with a mismatched grant_kind are refused. (c) Serde: legacy `{"kind":"approve-grant","command":"x"}` deserializes with None fields; a command with None fields serializes with no grant_kind/request_seq key; a legacy approve with neither field still approves by target.
5. Add one line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md.

GATES, run bare with no pipes: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and the numstat check above showing 0 deletions. Name new bindings `authority`, never `token`. Commit your own work before reporting.

features.title: REST grant routes refuse a decision for a superseded request
features.spec:
CONTEXT. The dashboard posts grant decisions to `POST /api/missions/:id/grant/approve` and `/grant/deny` (crates/server/src/rest.rs ~1180-1229). Bodies: `GrantApproveBody { command }`, `GrantDenyBody { command, reason (default 'denied by operator') }`, serde camelCase. `require_pending_grant` (~1343-1363) folds the log and returns 409 (`ApiError::conflict`) only when the text differs or nothing is pending; then the handler enqueues ControlCommand::ApproveGrant/DenyGrant and returns 202 `{queued:true}`. Earlier features in this mission added (crates/engine/src/types.rs): `PendingGrantRequest.request_seq: Option<u64>` (wire requestSeq) and optional `grant_kind: Option<GrantKind>` / `request_seq: Option<u64>` on ControlCommand::ApproveGrant/DenyGrant, re-checked by the engine at drain time. rest.rs currently passes None. Read those definitions first.

DO:
1. Add optional `kind: Option<GrantKind>` and `request_seq: Option<u64>` (wire kind / requestSeq, `#[serde(default)]`) to both body structs; `kind` is safe here because these structs are not tagged.
2. Extend require_pending_grant to take these Options. When provided, kind must equal the pending kind and requestSeq must equal the pending request_seq; on mismatch return 409 with a message containing 'superseded' naming what is pending (seq and kind) and enqueue nothing. Keep the command-text check. Omitted fields keep today's behaviour (the CLI and the experimental Even G2 client keep working).
3. Forward the provided values into the enqueued ControlCommand's grant_kind and request_seq.
4. Do NOT edit crates/engine/src/types.rs or any other engine contract file.
5. TESTS in crates/server/tests/host_test.rs (reuse `seed_pending_grant_log` ~1239; see `grant_routes_enqueue_approve_and_deny_decisions` ~1264). Every new test name must contain `superseded_grant`. (a) Pending requestSeq is N; approve and deny with the same command but requestSeq != N each return 409 and the control directory gains no file. (b) A kind mismatch returns 409. (c) Matching requestSeq and kind returns 202 and the enqueued control carries request_seq Some(N) and the grant_kind. (d) A legacy body with only command still returns 202. (e) GET /api/missions/:id/state exposes pendingGrantRequest.requestSeq.
6. Add one line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md.

features.title: Slack grant buttons carry the request's sequence number and kind
features.spec:
CONTEXT. Slack grant cards are built by `build_grant_ready` (crates/slack/src/format.rs ~897). Both buttons (action ids `kranz_approve_grant` / `kranz_deny_grant`, format.rs ~44/48) carry `value = format!("{}:{}", mission_id, command)` (~898), capped at MAX_BUTTON_VALUE. `GrantReady { mission_id, milestone_id, kind, command }` (format.rs ~221) has no seq; it is built in crates/slack/src/outbound.rs ~165-169 inside the GrantRequested arm of classify (where `event.seq` is in hand), plus test literals at outbound.rs ~450 and outbound_engine.rs ~786; production call outbound_engine.rs ~586. Clicks are parsed by `parse_grant_button_value` (crates/slack/src/inbound.rs ~647, split on first ':') into `Action::ApproveGrant/DenyGrant { mission_id, command, user_id, response_url }` (inbound.rs ~309/316, routed ~534-555), dispatched in crates/slack/src/dispatch.rs ~918-958 to `grant_control` then `enqueue_grant_control` (crates/slack/src/bridge.rs ~2399-2460), which compares only `pending.command == command`. Refusals are already sent ephemerally via reply_ephemeral ('Couldn't queue grant command: {e}', bridge.rs ~2423-2431). Old cards stay clickable. Earlier features added `PendingGrantRequest.request_seq: Option<u64>` and optional `grant_kind`/`request_seq` on ControlCommand::ApproveGrant/DenyGrant (crates/engine/src/types.rs). Do NOT edit any engine file.

DO:
1. Add `request_seq: u64` to GrantReady, filled from `event.seq` where the card is built.
2. Encode the button value as `{mission_id}:{request_seq}:{kind}:{command}` (kind = GrantKind's kebab-case wire name). Mission ids, the decimal seq and kebab kinds contain no ':', so split on the first three ':'; the command may contain ':'. Apply the existing MAX_BUTTON_VALUE and visibility rules to the full new value.
3. parse_grant_button_value returns mission, seq, kind and command. A legacy `mission:command` value (no numeric seq plus known kind) must NOT become a decision: reply ephemerally that the card is out of date (use the newest card or the dashboard) and enqueue nothing.
4. Add `request_seq: u64` and `grant_kind: GrantKind` to Action::ApproveGrant and DenyGrant. Repo lesson: grep and update EVERY construction and match site before reporting — inbound.rs (routing ~534-555, tests ~1740-1790), dispatch.rs (exhaustive match in dispatch_action ~37, arms ~918/938), bridge.rs (exhaustive apply_action ~1205, arms ~1238-1239), and crates/slack/tests/*.rs.
5. enqueue_grant_control compares seq and kind as well as command with the pending request; on mismatch bail with a message containing 'superseded' that names the pending request (shown to the clicker, nothing enqueued). On match enqueue with `grant_kind: Some(..)` and `request_seq: Some(..)`.
6. TESTS; every new test name must contain `superseded_grant`: (a) format/parse round trip with a command containing ':'; (b) a button for seq N while seq M is pending with the SAME text is refused and the mission's control directory gains no file; (c) a kind mismatch is refused; (d) a legacy `mission:command` value is refused and enqueues nothing; (e) a matching click enqueues a control carrying request_seq and grant_kind. Update existing tests (`grant_ready_names_the_command_with_approve_deny_buttons`, `block_actions_grant_buttons_route_to_grant_actions`, `grant_requested_classifies_grant_ready`, other grant_card/grant_ready tests) only as the new format requires.
7. Add one line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md.

GATES, run bare: `cargo test -p kranz-slack` (must COMPILE and pass in full), `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`. Commit your own work before reporting.

features.title: Board polling stops with a visible paused state after an authentication failure
features.spec:
CONTEXT (confirmed). src/components/BoardLens.tsx in the dashboard (apps/dashboard) polls on two window.setInterval timers (~246-252): lists every LIST_POLL_MS = 10s via `refreshLists` (~193-209) → store `loadTickets()`/`loadMissions()` (src/lib/store.ts ~351-393) → api.tickets()/api.missions(); and per-running-mission state every STATE_POLL_MS = 5s via `fetchRunningStates` (~161-191) → `api.missionState(id)`. It also refreshes on visibilitychange (~254-263). None pass options, so on a 401 (off-loopback or read-auth serve, token missing or rejected) `getJson` (src/lib/api.ts ~142-164) calls `awaitToken()` (src/lib/token.ts ~143) and parks a new waiter. CONSTRAINT: the existing test BoardLens.test.tsx ~982 requires Board files to reference only `api.missionState` among api methods, so route the opt-out through `api.missionState(id, opts)` and store-level options, not new direct api calls from BoardLens.

On the first token-required failure BoardLens enters a paused state: clear both intervals, ignore visibility refreshes, issue no further poll requests. features.title: An expired permission card holds its place
features.spec:
CONTEXT (confirmed). src/components/PermissionRequestPanel.tsx in the dashboard (apps/dashboard) re-renders every second via `useNow()` (src/lib/useNow.ts) and maps over `pendingPermissions(state, now)` (src/lib/pendingAsks.ts ~44-53), which drops records whose `proposal.deadline` has passed (the engine also later marks them closed with reason 'deadline expired'). So when a request expires its whole `
` card unmounts and every panel and button below it moves up under the cursor; with two permission cards, the second card's 'Allow once' can land where the first one's was. The panel is mounted in src/App.tsx's right column (~142) and BoardLens's act column (~551-562). Compare src/components/GateReviewPanel.tsx, which keeps an expired attempt in place with a status message. DO: 1. A card this panel has rendered as pending stays mounted in the same position after its deadline passes, including when the record later arrives closed because it expired. Its Allow and Deny buttons become disabled and clicking them sends nothing. 2. The card has a status line that is ALWAYS rendered, in both states, as the same element (e.g. `

`): a non-breaking space while pending, text containing 'Expired' (e.g. 'Expired — no answer was sent') afterwards. Nothing is inserted into or removed from the card at the moment of expiry. Give the line a reserved min-height in src/styles.css. Any existing conditional status lines inside the card that could appear at expiry must not change the card's height at that moment. 3. An expired card leaves only when the operator dismisses it via a 'Dismiss' button placed inside the reserved status line (not where Allow/Deny sit), or when the selected mission changes. 4. A request already expired, resolved or closed when first rendered is still not shown, so the existing test `it.each(['expired','resolved','closed'])('hides a %s request')` keeps passing. Do NOT change `pendingPermissions` semantics (BoardLens ask counts and src/lib/pendingAsks.test.ts rely on them); keep retained-card logic local to the panel or in a new selector. TESTS in src/components/PermissionRequestPanel.test.tsx (vitest + @testing-library/react + jsdom; api mocked; drive time with fake timers or by mocking useNow). Every new test name must contain the tag `DD4` (no existing test contains it). Render two pending cards; capture the first card's section, its status element and buttons, and the second card's buttons. Advance past the first card's deadline only, then assert: the same DOM nodes are still connected and in the same order; the status element is the same node and reads Expired; the first card's buttons are disabled and clicking Allow does not call api.answerPermission; the second card's buttons are the same nodes and still enabled. The test must fail on the current code. Add one line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md. Rebuild and commit the embedded bundle: `npm --prefix apps/dashboard ci`, `npm --prefix apps/dashboard run build`, `npm --prefix apps/dashboard run sync-embedded`, then commit crates/cli/assets/dashboard/dist. GATES, run bare: `npm --prefix apps/dashboard test`, `npm --prefix apps/dashboard run build`, `npm --prefix apps/dashboard run check-embedded`, `npm --prefix apps/dashboard run lint`. Commit your own work before reporting.
validationCriteria: A permission card shown as pending keeps its DOM node and position after its deadline, with Allow and Deny disabled and the always-present status line reading Expired (test name contains DD4)
Clicking an expired card's Allow sends no answer (test name contains DD4)
A sibling permission card's buttons keep their DOM nodes, order and enabled state when another card expires (test name contains DD4)
A request already expired, resolved or closed at first render is still hidden (existing test passes)
Dashboard test, build, check-embedded and lint pass, and the embedded bundle is committed

consideredAlternatives.chosen: One milestone with eight independent features in dependency order: two small engine features (record the request seq; bind and check ControlCommand), then the REST, Slack and dashboard consumers, then the three dashboard-only stability fixes. This redrafts the approved m-fcde79 plan on a base that carries #191, splitting its oversize engine feature (flagged by the context-fit check at 5446 chars / 27 files) in two. The repo runs the whole contract at every milestone gate, so one milestone avoids waiver rounds. kind/requestSeq are optional on REST and in the engine so the CLI and Even G2 keep working, while the dashboard and Slack always bind and legacy Slack card values are refused. Engine contract fields are inserted as new lines only, and ControlCommand fields are named grant_kind/request_seq to avoid its serde tag 'kind'.
